Report Description
///THIS REPORT WAS RECEIVED VIA THE WEB REPORTING TOOL.///ON NOV. 9, 2013 MY HUSBAND AND I WERE WALKING ON THE BEACH (GULF SIDE) EAST OF THE FT. PICKENS ENTRANCE AT THE GULF ISLANDS NATIONAL SEASHORE. DIRECTLY IN FRONT OF THE RANGER STATION WE SAW, EMBEDDED IN THE SAND, AN AMORPHOUSLY SHAPED "TAR BALL) APPROX. 18 IN. LONG AND 7 IN. WIDE. IT WAS COMPRISED OF TAR AND VEGETATIVE MATTER. CONTINUING EAST, THE LENGTH OF ABOUT ONE AND ONE-HALF FOOTBALL FIELDS EAST OF THE RANGER STATION WE CAME ACROSS A STRUCTURE HEAVILY COATED IN TAR. IT LAY ON THE SHORE, DIRECTLY BEHIND A TREE STUMP IN THE SHALLOW WATER. AT FIRST GLANCE, IT APPEARED TO BE SOME KIND OF REEF OR STONE STRUCTURE. ON CLOSER INSPECTION, WE OBSERVED THAT, WHATEVER IT HAD BEEN, IT WAS NOW HEAVILY COATED IN TAR, WITH VEGETATIVE MATTER EMBEDDED AND CLINGING TO IT.

properties.summary: Incident Type: STORAGE TANK - NRC Report ID: 1073217 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: NC CORRECTIONAL INSTITUTION FOR WOMEN
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1073217
Incident Time: 2014-02-03 08:30:00
Nearest City: Raleigh, NC
Location: REAR OF NC CORRECTIONAL INSTITUTION FOR WOMEN PROPERTY 1034 BRAGG STREET
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: OIL, FUEL: NO. 2-D
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: NC CORRECTIONAL INSTITUTION FOR WOMEN
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 35.767222, -78.620278 (Explicit)
Reported Spill Volume: 3151 gallon
Report Description
****WEB REPORT**** A PRESSURIZED UNDERGROUND LINE RETURNING FUEL OIL FROM A BOILER TO AN ABOVEGROUND STORAGE TANK IS BELIEVED TO HAVE LEAKED DURING AN APPROXIMATELY 6 HOUR AND 15 MINUTE WINDOW OF OPERATION. NO. 2 FUEL OIL SEEPED UP TO THE GROUND SURFACE AND WAS THEN FLUSHED DOWN HILLSIDE DRAINAGE WAYS BY MELTING SNOW AND RAIN INTO A WET-WEATHER IMPOUNDMENT POND AT THE REAR OF THE PRISON PROPERTY WITH A SMALL AMOUNT OF OIL ESCAPING THE PROPERTY AND ENTERING WALNUT CREEK. A SHEEN WAS NOTICED IN THE CREEK. FACILITY MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL INVESTIGATED AND DISCOVERED THE OIL LEAK SOURCE AND NOTIFIED UP THE CHAIN OF COMMAND AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE CLEAN-UP EFFORTS WERE INITIATED. LOCAL AND STATE ENVIRONMENTAL AGENCIES WERE NOTIFIED. OIL-ABSORBENT BOOMS WERE PLACED ACROSS THE DISCHARGE POINT INTO WALNUT CREEK AND ALSO ACROSS WALNUT CREEK AND THERE IS NO FURTHER EVIDENCE OF OIL FROM THIS INCIDENT ENTERING WALNUT CREEK.
